blocks.content: A dendritic pattern develops where the river channel follows the slope of the terrain and resembles the branches of a tree.

rows: Uniformly resistant rocks and gentle slope
Alternating parallel bands of hard and soft rock
Tributaries join main streams at right angles
Old folded mountain regions of Chota Nagpur Plateau

items: Himalayan rivers like the Indus, Sutlej, and Brahmaputra are classic examples of antecedent drainage that predate the Himalayan orogeny.
Amarkantak Plateau is frequently cited in exams as the primary Indian example of a radial drainage pattern giving rise to the Narmada and Son rivers.
Loktak Lake in Manipur is the prime example of centripetal drainage where surrounding streams drain into a central lake basin.
Trellis patterns form in folded sedimentary structures where primary tributaries flow parallel to folded ridges and secondary tributaries join at right angles.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Consequent streams follow the natural slope of the terrain, forming the initial drainage network of a newly uplifted landform.
Antecedent rivers existed before the upliftment of mountains and maintained their courses by cutting deep gorges through rising landmasses.
Dendritic drainage patterns develop in areas of uniform rock structure and resemble the branching network of a tree.
Radial drainage patterns emerge when rivers radiate outwards in all directions from a central elevated peak or dome.
Centripetal drainage occurs when streams flow from surrounding high grounds into a central depression, lake, or inland basin.
